BiblicalUsage: Hanameel was the son of Shallum, Jeremiah's uncle, and his name is tied to the field at Anathoth. He came to Jeremiah in the prison court saying buy my field, for the right of redemption is yours. Jeremiah bought it, weighed the silver, and gave the evidence of the purchase to Baruch before the witnesses.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Hanameel's field is the most hopeful purchase in the Bible: Jeremiah bought land in a country about to fall, because God had said houses and fields would be possessed again. The cousin who sold it did not know it, but his field became a sermon.
